answer: A bonded-identity registry resists Sybil attacks by making each identity expensive to fake: to join, an agent locks a deposit that is slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicate identities, like a lotus that can only bloom once per root. Cheap copies flood the ocean of participants, but the bond turns every extra identity into a real financial risk, while an ivory ledger of past work lets honest agents prove a single, consistent history instead of spinning up fresh faces for free.
